subject: Latency degradations and proposed interim remediation for SummitWorks
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@summitworks.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@summitworks.com
Date: 2026-11-19T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Latency spike Nov 12–15 — remediation & compensation request

Markus / Karthik,

We experienced recurring tail-latency spikes and a pronounced throughput degradation between Nov 12 and Nov 15 that impacted our user-facing search flows. Our telemetry shows p95 tail spikes up to ~1.8s (baseline ~220ms) and a 22% increase in median CPU throttling for our inference requests (attached is our usage report for the window). This materially affected a small subset of paying customers and triggered a partial outage of some background batch jobs.

Can you confirm:
- Whether there is a known root cause on Redwood's side for the Nov 12–15 window?
- What short-term remediation you can commit to (configuration or routing changes)?
- Whether Redwood will consider a billing make-good or one-off credit for the impacted window while we validate the fix?

Procurement asked that we get an estimate of the remedy/goodwill you can offer so we can present to our CFO. Happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Platform, SummitWorks
Elena.Park@summitworks.com
Attachment: summitworks_usage_report.csv

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@summitworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike Nov 12–15 — remediation & compensation request

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed note and the CSV. I've kicked off an internal triage and asked our infra team to pull the serving traces for the Nov 12–15 window. Initial hypothesis: automated autoscaler behavior combined with a model-version rotation created intermittent cold-cache penalties on a small subset of hosts. We're verifying.

Short term we can:
- Route your critical traffic to dedicated capacity pool for the next 72 hours to stabilize tail latency (low friction, but will increase your short-term run rate).
- Apply a temporary KV-cache pinning config and bump prewarm tokens for the affected model to reduce cold starts.

On the commercial side I'm prepared to propose an interim goodwill concession while we complete the deeper post-mortem. To move quickly, can you confirm the financial owner at SummitWorks (CFO or procurement contact) and whether you prefer a percent-based credit for the Nov invoice or a fixed-dollar credit applied to the next invoice?

I attached a short diagnostic request PDF with the logs/ID slices that would help our SREs. If you can upload those, we can close the loop faster.

I'll loop in Karthik to provide a range for the commercial concession we can offer without exec sign-off, and leave him to propose an authorization path if we need an exception.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_diagnostic_request.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Latency spike Nov 12–15 — remediation & compensation request

Markus — quick internal note. I ran a conservative revenue impact estimate based on the usage CSV and SummitWorks' pricing band. Two realistic offer shapes:

Option A (conservative): One-month credit capped at $50,000 applied to the Dec invoice. This is a visible remedial offer and keeps customer retention risk low.
Option B (targeted): Fixed $30,000 one-off credit specific to the Nov usage window (smaller, faster signoff).

Operationally, we should require a short remediation acceptance (a checklist: dedicated routing for core flows for 30 days + post-mortem within 2 weeks) as a condition for the credit. Either option will need Marissa's authorization if we exceed the $25k delegated limit. I've attached a quick calc with the ROI hit and ledger impact.

If Markus wants to extend a split option (e.g., $15k plus credits for next month), that's doable but will need clear heads-up to finance. Let me know what you want me to prep for exec sign-off.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: credit_estimate_calc.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike Nov 12–15 — remediation & compensation request

Thanks for the context and the calc. Authorizing a one-off concession in this case is reasonable given SummitWorks' ARR band and the operational impact described. Approval: authorize a $35,000 credit to be applied against the customer's Dec 2026 invoice, conditional on the customer accepting the remediation checklist and scheduling a 2-week post-mortem with our SREs.

Conditions and notes for the external comms:
- The credit is a one-time goodwill adjustment and is not a precedent for future incidents.
- We require a remediation acceptance doc (I can review a short acceptance statement) and a post-mortem within 14 calendar days of the remediation work.
- Finance will apply the credit after we receive a signed acceptance form; we need procurement on the distribution list.

Markus — please send the external confirmation and include the acceptance link (DocuSign) and the remediation plan Drive link. Copy Legal if you want a standard language.

-Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood_credit_term_sheet.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@summitworks.com>, procurement@summitworks.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, legal@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Resolution: goodwill credit & remediation plan for Nov 12–15 latency window

Hi Elena — following our internal review and Marissa's approval, Redwood will provide a one-time $35,000 credit to be applied against SummitWorks' Dec 2026 invoice. This credit is contingent on SummitWorks signing the brief remediation acceptance (DocuSign link below) and scheduling a 2-week post-mortem with our SRE team.

Summary of next steps:
- SummitWorks to sign the remediation acceptance: https://docusign.example/sign/4f7a9
- SRE-led post-mortem: we propose Nov 25, 10:00 PT; please confirm or suggest an alternative.
- We will route your critical production traffic to the dedicated capacity pool within 4 hours of acceptance to stabilize tail latency during the remediation window.
- Finance will apply the $35,000 credit after we receive the signed acceptance document (applies to Dec 2026 invoice).

I appreciate your patience while we validated the issue. Karthik will be your day-to-day contact for execution; Marissa's team will coordinate the credit application. If you want Legal to review the acceptance language, I have looped them in.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
